Using the reflection’s bounds and summing over \(b\) gives
\[
T(n)=
\begin{cases}
\left\lfloor \dfrac{n^2+24}{48}\right\rfloor, & n \text{ even},\\[4pt]
\left\lfloor \dfrac{(n+3)^2+24}{48}\right\rfloor, & n \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\]
Since \(n\) is the answer, we need \(T(n)=n\).

- If \(n\) is even, \(T(n)=n\) requires
  \[
  n\le \frac{n^2+24}{48}<n+1,
  \]
  which forces \(n=48\).

- If \(n\) is odd, the analogous inequalities force both \(n\ge 43\) and \(n\le 41\), impossible.

Thus the only positive solution is \(n=48\).

\[
\boxed{48}
\]
